    • minimizeEqualityConstrained

      public static <C extends Constraint & Jacobian> OptimizeResult minimizeEqualityConstrained(Function<Matrix,Double> fun, Function<Matrix,Matrix> grad, Function<Matrix,Matrix> hess, Matrix x0, C eq, int maxIter, double xtol, double gtol)
      Convenience entry point covering the equality-constrained slice of the trust-constr API: a scalar objective with an explicit gradient and Hessian, subject to optional pure-equality constraints from a single LinearConstraint or NonlinearConstraint.

      This is a focused subset of scipy.optimize.minimize(method='trust-constr') intended for problems where every constraint row is an equality (lb[i] == ub[i]). It dispatches to EqualityConstrainedSQP.eqSQP(de.labathome.trustconstr.interfaces.IFunctionAndConstraint, de.labathome.trustconstr.interfaces.IGradientAndJacobian, de.labathome.trustconstr.interfaces.LagrangeHessian, de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix, double, de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix, de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix, de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix, de.labathome.trustconstr.interfaces.StoppingCriterion, de.labathome.trustconstr.records.State, double, double, de.labathome.trustconstr.enums.ProjectionMethod, de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix, de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix, de.labathome.trustconstr.interfaces.LinearOperator) directly without the full canonical-form constraint pipeline. Callers with inequalities, Bounds, multiple constraints, or finite-difference Hessians/Jacobians should wait for the full minimizeTrustConstr(java.util.function.ToDoubleBiFunction<de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix, java.lang.Object>, de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix, java.lang.Object, java.util.function.BiFunction<de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix, java.lang.Object, de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix>, java.util.function.BiFunction<de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix, java.lang.Object, de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix>, de.labathome.trustconstr.interfaces.HessianProduct, de.labathome.trustconstr.records.Bounds, java.lang.Object, double, double, double, java.util.Optional<java.lang.Boolean>, de.labathome.trustconstr.interfaces.IterationCallback, int, int, de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix, double, double, double, double, de.labathome.trustconstr.enums.ProjectionMethod, boolean) orchestrator.

      Type Parameters:
      C - constraint type, must implement both Constraint and Jacobian
      Parameters:
      fun - objective function f : R^n -> R
      grad - analytic gradient g : R^n -> R^n
      hess - analytic Hessian H : R^n -> R^{n x n}
      x0 - initial point as a column vector (n x 1)
      eq - equality constraint, or null for unconstrained problems (the constraint object must satisfy nIneq() == 0)
      maxIter - maximum number of outer iterations
      xtol - stop when trustRadius < xtol
      gtol - stop when optimality < gtol and constrViolation < gtol
      Returns:
      populated OptimizeResult

      public static <C extends Constraint & Jacobian> OptimizeResult minimize(Function<Matrix,Double> fun, Function<Matrix,Matrix> grad, Function<Matrix,Matrix> hess, Matrix x0, C constraint, int maxIter, double xtol, double gtol)
      General-purpose entry point: routes to minimizeEqualityConstrained(java.util.function.Function<de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix, java.lang.Double>, java.util.function.Function<de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix, de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix>, java.util.function.Function<de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix, de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix>, de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix, C, int, double, double) when the constraint has only equality rows, and to a TrustRegionInteriorPoint-driven path when any inequality rows are present. Pure unconstrained problems route through the equality path with an empty constraint set.

      Like minimizeEqualityConstrained(java.util.function.Function<de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix, java.lang.Double>, java.util.function.Function<de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix, de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix>, java.util.function.Function<de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix, de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix>, de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix, C, int, double, double), this is a focused subset of the full scipy.optimize.minimize(method='trust-constr') API: a single LinearConstraint or NonlinearConstraint (or null), no Bounds, no callback, no finite-difference Hessians/Jacobians.

    • minimize

      public static <C extends Constraint & Jacobian> OptimizeResult minimize(Function<Matrix,Double> fun, Function<Matrix,Matrix> grad, Matrix x0, C constraint, int maxIter, double xtol, double gtol)
      Convenience overload that approximates the objective Hessian via a fresh BFGS update strategy -- the scipy-default behaviour when hess is omitted from the user call.

      The BFGS update is driven manually inside the lagrHess closure: every time the SQP / IP outer loop asks for a fresh Lagrangian Hessian (i.e. after a successful step), we compare the current x and gradient to the previous values and call HessianUpdateStrategy.update(de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix, de.labathome.trustconstr.matrix.Matrix) to refresh the approximation.

      Type Parameters:
      C - constraint type, must implement Constraint and Jacobian
      Parameters:
      fun - objective function f : R^n -> R
      grad - analytic gradient g : R^n -> R^n
      x0 - initial point (n x 1)
      constraint - single constraint or null
      maxIter - maximum outer iterations
      xtol - stop when trustRadius < xtol
      gtol - stop when optimality < gtol and constrViolation < gtol
      Returns:
      populated OptimizeResult

    • minimizeTrustConstr

      public static OptimizeResult minimizeTrustConstr(ToDoubleBiFunction<Matrix,Object> fun, Matrix x0, Object args, BiFunction<Matrix,Object,Matrix> grad, BiFunction<Matrix,Object,Matrix> hess, HessianProduct hessp, Bounds bounds, Object constraints, double xTol, double gTol, double barrierTol, Optional<Boolean> sparseJacobian, IterationCallback callback, int maxIter, int verbose, Matrix finiteDifferenceRelStep, double initialConstraintPenalty, double initialTrustRadius, double initialBarrierParameter, double initialBarrierTolerance, ProjectionMethod factorizationMethod, boolean disp)
      Minimize a scalar function subject to constraints. Full scipy-shape entry point: see Conn, Gould & Toint, Trust Region Methods (SIAM, 2000), p.19 for the algorithm and parameter recommendations.
      Parameters:
      fun - objective (x, args) -> f(x)
      x0 - starting point (n x 1)
      args - extra arguments forwarded to fun/grad/hess; may be null
      grad - gradient (x, args) -> gradf(x); if null, computed by 2-point finite differences
      hess - Hessian (x, args) -> grad^2f(x); if null, approximated by BFGS
      hessp - Hessian-vector product; honored when hess is null (materialised via HessianLinearOperator)
      bounds - box bounds on x; folded into the constraint set as a LinearConstraint; may be null
      constraints - either a single LinearConstraint / NonlinearConstraint, an Object[] of such, or null
      xTol - tolerance for termination by change in x: stop when tr_radius < xTol
      gTol - tolerance for termination by Lagrangian gradient norm and constraint violation
      barrierTol - IP-only: termination requires barrier parameter below this threshold
      sparseJacobian - true/false forces all constraint Jacobians to that representation via SparsityForcedConstraint; Optional.empty() uses the constraint's native auto-detect
      callback - per-iteration callback; return true to terminate. May be null
      maxIter - maximum outer iterations
      verbose - verbosity level (0 silent, 1 termination report, 2-3 per-iteration progress)
      finiteDifferenceRelStep - relative step size for FD gradient/Hessian; may be null
      initialConstraintPenalty - initial constraint penalty for the merit function f(x) + rho ||c(x)||_2
      initialTrustRadius - initial trust-region radius
      initialBarrierParameter - IP-only: initial barrier parameter for the log-barrier subproblem
      initialBarrierTolerance - IP-only: initial inner-loop tolerance for the barrier subproblem
      factorizationMethod - how to factor the equality-Jacobian for the projection: one of AUGMENTED_SYSTEM, QR_FACTORIZATION, SVD_FACTORIZATION, or null for auto-select (QR for dense, AUGMENTED_SYSTEM for sparse)
      disp - if true, bumps verbose to 1 when it was 0
      Returns:
      populated OptimizeResult

    • minimizeTrustConstr

      public static OptimizeResult minimizeTrustConstr(ToDoubleBiFunction<Matrix,Object> fun, Matrix x0, Object args, BiFunction<Matrix,Object,Matrix> grad, BiFunction<Matrix,Object,Matrix> hess, HessianProduct hessp, Bounds bounds, Object constraints, double xTol, double gTol, double barrierTol, Optional<Boolean> sparseJacobian, IterationCallback callback, int maxIter, int verbose, Matrix finiteDifferenceRelStep, double initialConstraintPenalty, double initialTrustRadius, double initialBarrierParameter, double initialBarrierTolerance, ProjectionMethod factorizationMethod, boolean disp, ExecutorService workers)
      Strict scipy _minimize_trustregion_constr(..., workers=N) counterpart. Same arguments as minimizeTrustConstr(ToDoubleBiFunction, Matrix, Object, BiFunction, BiFunction, HessianProduct, Bounds, Object, double, double, double, Optional, IterationCallback, int, int, Matrix, double, double, double, double, ProjectionMethod, boolean), plus a final ExecutorService for parallel FD evaluation.

      workers only affects the FD-gradient path (when grad is null); analytic gradients are unaffected.

      Parameters:
      fun - objective (x, args) -> f
      x0 - starting iterate (n x 1)
      args - extra arguments forwarded to fun/grad/hess
      grad - analytic gradient (x, args) -> grad f(x), or null for FD
      hess - analytic Hessian (x, args) -> H(x), or null for BFGS
      hessp - matrix-free Hessian-vector product (x, p, args) -> H(x) p, or null
      bounds - box bounds on the decision variables, or null
      constraints - LinearConstraint, NonlinearConstraint, Object[] mix, or null
      xTol - step-size convergence tolerance
      gTol - KKT-optimality convergence tolerance
      barrierTol - IP-path barrier-parameter convergence tolerance
      sparseJacobian - forces sparse / dense Jacobian; Optional.empty() auto-detects
      callback - per-iteration callback, returns true to terminate; null disables
      maxIter - iteration limit
      verbose - verbosity level (0 silent, 1 progress table)
      finiteDifferenceRelStep - FD relative step (per-element vector); null uses the eps-derived default
      initialConstraintPenalty - initial merit-function penalty
      initialTrustRadius - initial trust-region radius
      initialBarrierParameter - IP-path: initial barrier coefficient
      initialBarrierTolerance - IP-path: initial barrier-subproblem tolerance
      factorizationMethod - projection factorisation; null picks QR for dense / AugmentedSystem for sparse
      disp - bumps verbose to 1 when it was 0
      workers - executor for parallel FD evaluation; null = serial
      Returns:
      populated OptimizeResult
